nodes.label: Algerian CRM: Technology Decisions v0.2
nodes.rationale: Decision records per topic (options, pick, why, when to revisit); supersedes v0.1; companion to CRM_Algeria_V1_Specification.pdf

nodes.label: Microservices, Event-Driven Architecture
nodes.rationale: User's decision (driver D10, independent deployability and failure isolation); author disagrees and documents seven rules to make it survive; confidence [Likely] that modular monolith is lower risk

nodes.label: Modular Monolith (runner-up)
nodes.rationale: Author's recommended lower-risk path for V1: one codebase with same module boundaries for first three milestones, extracting services on evidence; avoids distributed-monolith failure mode

nodes.label: Seven Rules for Surviving Microservices
nodes.rationale: Services arrive with milestone; boundaries by data ownership; one service template; sync calls exception; contracts are code; observability before features; tripwires

nodes.label: Portability Hedge (Open Protocols Only, D2)
nodes.rationale: Legalities parked; managed services allowed only if they speak an open protocol with a self-hostable equivalent (Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, AMQP, S3, OTLP) so a forced move is a migration, not a rewrite

nodes.label: Service Boundary Tests (data ownership, consistency)
nodes.rationale: Split where seams are already eventual, merge where seams are transactional; order lifecycle and shipments stay in one service

nodes.label: identity-access service
nodes.rationale: M0; token issuer for everyone; owns users, sessions, MFA, businesses, members, permissions, invitations, API keys

nodes.label: crm service
nodes.rationale: M1; contacts, phones, tags, pipelines, opportunities, interactions, call logs, tasks; large stable dataset

nodes.label: orders service
nodes.rationale: M2; transactional core merging Sales and Logistics: order, shipment and return states change together

nodes.label: scoring service
nodes.rationale: M3; different data sensitivity, batch recompute, owns global layer; C# rules engine with versioned parameters and reason codes, ONNX later; GetScore/BatchGetScore over gRPC

nodes.label: integrations service
nodes.rationale: M4; absorbs third-party instability and webhook spikes; carrier, WhatsApp, Shopify, SMS, email adapters

nodes.label: messaging service
nodes.rationale: M5; long-lived connections scale differently; SignalR hub

nodes.label: presence service
nodes.rationale: M5; public profiles, reviews, reports; read-heavy public surface

nodes.label: platform service
nodes.rationale: Starts as shared library code; becomes a service when two or more services need the capability at runtime

nodes.label: Gateway (YARP)
nodes.rationale: Edge component: JWT validation, rate limiting, sid revocation check, public /v1 API with API keys

nodes.label: Nuxt BFF
nodes.rationale: Browser talks only to Nuxt origin with sealed HttpOnly session cookie; JWT never reaches browser JS; tokens in Valkey; single-flight refresh; CSRF via SameSite+Origin+custom header; one-time ticket for WebSocket

nodes.label: Database per Service
nodes.rationale: No shared tables, no cross-DB queries; logical DBs on one PostgreSQL cluster initially for cost; foreign IDs are opaque UUIDs validated by read models

nodes.label: Phone Pepper / phone_hash
nodes.rationale: Shared with crm, orders, scoring from secret store; conscious trade-off vs a synchronous resolve-identity call on every contact write

nodes.label: Local Read Model Fed by Events
gRPC (fresh-read queries only, one hop)
nodes.rationale: Chosen with restricted use: contract-first, deadlines; never changes another service's state; max one hop; deadline, retry only idempotent reads, circuit breaker, fallback; headless service for HTTP/2 load balancing

nodes.label: REST + OpenAPI Edge APIs
nodes.rationale: Standard for integrators and generated typed Nuxt client; gRPC from Nuxt rejected; JSON transcoding possible later

nodes.label: RabbitMQ (quorum queues)
nodes.rationale: Mature, per-message ack and DLX, open AMQP protocol (D2); Kafka runner-up (heavy ops); NATS not chosen; Azure Service Bus/SQS rejected as proprietary. Topology: topic exchange per producer, quorum queue per consumer per source

nodes.label: Transactional Outbox
nodes.rationale: Outbox in service DB, relay with publisher confirms, at-least-once delivery

nodes.label: Idempotent Consumers / Inbox
nodes.rationale: Inbox table keyed by (eventId, consumer); version guards for out-of-order delivery; bounded retries then dead-letter

nodes.label: Wolverine
nodes.rationale: Author's lean (MIT [Likely], built-in durable outbox/inbox with EF Core and RabbitMQ), conditional on spike S2; alternative is in-repo library over RabbitMQ.Client

nodes.label: MassTransit
nodes.rationale: Out unless budgeted: v9 commercial, v8 maintenance ends after 2026

nodes.label: CloudEvents-style Event Envelope
nodes.rationale: eventId, type, source, occurredAt, subject, tenantId, correlationId, causationId; JSON with JSON Schema per version, golden tests, additive-only; JSON for human-readable debugging

nodes.label: Choreography-first Flows (no saga engine)
nodes.rationale: Every flow is a chain of local transactions with compensating events; orchestrator only when multi-step compensation across services is needed

nodes.label: Service Template / ServiceDefaults
nodes.rationale: Single most important investment: OpenTelemetry, Serilog PII scrubbing, health, JWT/JWKS validation, tenant resolution, RLS tenant setting, outbox/inbox, resilience, Problem Details, OpenAPI, tests, Dockerfile/Helm, CI

nodes.label: .NET 10 LTS / ASP.NET Core
nodes.rationale: Supported until 14 Nov 2028 [Certain]

nodes.label: Licence and Supply-chain Watchlist
nodes.rationale: Avoid MediatR, AutoMapper, MassTransit v9, FluentAssertions, Duende (commercial); prefer Valkey over Redis; External Secrets/SOPS or OpenBao over Vault; PrimeVue core only. Driver D7

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Native RLS, jsonb, partial indexes, free and portable (D2, D4); vanilla features plus pg_trgm, unaccent only

nodes.label: Row-Level Security Multi-tenancy (business_id)
nodes.rationale: Policy business_id = current_setting('app.business_id'); set transaction-locally because session-level setting leaks through pooled connections; non-owner app role; EF Core global filters as second layer; tenant from event envelope in consumers

nodes.label: EF Core 10 (Npgsql) + Dapper
nodes.rationale: EF Core for commands, Dapper/raw SQL for reads; migrations as separate deployment step, never auto-migrate on startup

nodes.label: IFileStorage
nodes.rationale: No storage product named; implementations LocalDiskFileStorage, S3FileStorage (open S3 protocol), optional AzureBlobFileStorage; time-limited URLs, tenant-prefixed keys, async scan, soft delete

nodes.label: Valkey (Redis-compatible)
nodes.rationale: Cache, BFF session store, rate limiting, SignalR backplane, revocation list; needed from M0

nodes.label: Nuxt (Vue 3, TypeScript)
nodes.rationale: User's decision; Nitro server layer is a natural BFF; @nuxtjs/i18n per-locale dir rtl; PrimeVue supports Nuxt 4

nodes.label: PrimeVue
nodes.rationale: Documented native RTL via CSS logical properties (Carousel, Galleria exceptions); DataTable completeness is deciding factor; MIT core; Kanban and chat not provided

nodes.label: Arabic RTL / French i18n
nodes.rationale: Driver D5; Western digits for phones/prices/dates; self-hosted Arabic font

nodes.label: ASP.NET Core Identity + OpenIddict
nodes.rationale: OSS, standard OIDC/JWT, JWKS, refresh rotation, client credentials; Keycloak runner-up; Duende rejected (commercial); Auth0/Entra/Clerk rejected (proprietary)

nodes.label: JWT Token Design
nodes.rationale: 10-minute access token; claims sub, sid, tid (active business), role, perms/perm_ver, locale; token exchange on business switch; rotating refresh with reuse detection held by BFF; local JWKS validation; sid revocation set in Valkey

nodes.label: OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE Login
nodes.rationale: Identity-hosted localized pages; credentials never touch BFF; fallback headless login API decided after S1/S6

nodes.label: Carrier Adapters (Yalidine, ZR Express, Maystro, Ecotrack, Noest, E-com Delivery)
nodes.rationale: Direct typed adapters behind one interface, no aggregator so personal data stays with us; API shapes known only via third-party SDKs (R3)

nodes.label: WhatsApp Cloud API
nodes.rationale: Algeria priced market ~US$0.004 utility/auth; also used for phone verification; onboarding for Algerian entity unverified (R2)

nodes.label: Webhook Inbox
nodes.rationale: Every adapter uses inbox, signature verification, idempotent processing, retries and replay

nodes.label: Kubernetes (managed, GitOps)
nodes.rationale: Managed K8s with open-protocol data services recommended; self-managed k3s fallback; Docker Compose rejected for 6-8 services; PaaS rejected (D2). Helm/Kustomize, Argo CD/Flux, KEDA on queue depth, no mesh in V1

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry + Grafana Stack Observability
nodes.rationale: W3C trace context through HTTP, gRPC and RabbitMQ headers, stored in outbox row; Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Grafana; alerts on outbox age, DLQ depth, consumer lag

nodes.label: Quality Engineering Practices
nodes.rationale: xUnit, architecture tests, buf breaking + golden JSON contract tests, Testcontainers, cross-tenant tests, reliability tests, small E2E suite, k6 load

nodes.label: Spike S1: Walking Skeleton
nodes.rationale: 2 weeks: gateway + Nuxt BFF + identity-access + crm; OIDC login, JWT, session store, gRPC crm->identity, outbox->RabbitMQ->consumer, trace across hops, deployed to K8s; validates most of the microservices bet

nodes.label: Architecture Tripwires
nodes.rationale: Agreed in advance after M2: >30% time on plumbing, lead time >1 day, >2-hop chains or cross-service transactions, services changing together, heavy local dev. Remedy: merge services, extend template, reconsider modular monolith

nodes.label: Global Cross-business Score (feature-flagged)
nodes.rationale: Behind global_score_visible flag for product reason: shared negative-behaviour score invites sabotage and false reports; legal review R1 before enabling
